attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. The device-building part is framed as reported; the uploading part is his own assertion.

semantics.note: Keeps 'reportedly' for the device development and treats 'no doubt' as Marcus's own firm claim about uploading. 'Everything you say' is kept as he wrote it. It is a claim about the present state, so observation is the right kind.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. '24x7 monitoring' means continuous ambient sensing, and 'everything you say' means comprehensive cloud transmission of speech. It correctly says missing specifications do not contradict the claim and that both parts are needed for support.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own May 2025 disclosure confirms design work with Ive. It says nothing about continuous monitoring or how speech is handled.

October 2025 secondary account of FT reporting. It describes a device intended for continuous sensing with unresolved privacy safeguards, which supports the 'reportedly building' part. It does not show that all speech is uploaded to the cloud.

reviews.rationale: Credible reporting (e2) supports the claim that OpenAI was reportedly developing a continuously aware device, so that part holds. No device-specific disclosure or technical test shows whether all speech is sent to the cloud, and nothing contradicts it either. The contract requires both parts for support, and missing specifications are not a contradiction. The packet therefore does not settle the uploading part, so the outcome is unresolved.
